memo.body_markdown:
Recommendation

Prioritize the billing/support area this quarter, focusing first on the Free tier forced shuffle and skip limits issue and adjacent billing-support friction. Specifically: (1) Fix or relax the forced-shuffle / strict-skip behavior (billing.free_tier_restrictions), and (2) surface clearer messaging and settings around free-tier limitations and upgrade options to reduce confusion and antagonism.

Evidence

- The top-ranked issue by our baseline priority (complaint_count x mean_severity = severity_sum) is billing.free_tier_restrictions: complaint_count 11 [C01], severity_sum 33 [C02], mean_severity 3.000000 [C03], priority_score 33 [C04], cancellation_intent_members 1 [C05].
- At the area level, billing_support shows complaints 12 [A2COM], severity_sum 35 [A2SEV], cancellations 1 [A2CAN], mean_severity 2.916667 [A2MEA], indicating concentrated negative feedback tied to billing/support topics.
- Representative user remarks (selected short quotes): `88439ec2-7c49-4c57-bedb-c5e098692aff` ("I'll switch"), `d146397f-4a94-4980-be00-ae9212eca3a7` ("can't even pick"), `e5e6c55f-3069-4b7c-9807-f8b5d5bf2726` ("Too many ads...."), `9e5f9745-f8be-48d3-b9de-4d118507d94a` ("can't even go back").

Why this vs. other areas

- Usability: the usability area has complaints 12 [A3COM] and severity_sum 27 [A3SEV], but its top individual usability issue (ads) has priority_score 16 [C14] (complaint_count 8 [C11], severity_sum 16 [C12]). That is meaningfully lower than the billing free-tier priority_score 33 [C04], so incremental impact per effort is likely larger in billing/support.

- Playback: the playback area shows complaints 6 [A4COM] and severity_sum 20 [A4SEV], with the top playback crash/freeze issue at priority_score 8 [C29] (complaint_count 2 [C26], severity_sum 8 [C27]). While playback has a higher mean severity 3.333333 [A4MEA] and sev4plus 2 [A4SEV], its lower volume keeps it behind billing_support by the priority metric.

- Access: access area has complaints 2 [A5COM] and severity_sum 8 [A5SEV], with access.login_failure at priority_score 8 [C24] (complaint_count 2 [C21], severity_sum 8 [C22]). Access shows high mean_severity 4.000000 [A5MEA] and sev4plus 2 [A5SEV], but the low complaint volume means fewer reviews drive priority compared with the billing issue.

Risks and limitations

- Data are self-selected Google Play reviews (May 2022–Nov 2023) and are not a representative customer sample; do not infer population rates, causal churn, or revenue impact. Cancellation language is stated intent only.
- Labels and severity come from a small model with verifier agreement limits (see method notes); severity labeling has uncertainty. The baseline priority uses severity_sum; if severity labeling shifts, priority ordering could change.
- Coverage metrics: source_rows 100 [K01], completed_records 100 [K02], quarantined_records 0 [K03], pending_records 0 [K04], empty_text_quarantines 0 [K05].

What would change the recommendation

- If additional data showed higher-volume or higher-severity playback or access incidents (new crash spikes or widespread login failures), their severity_sum or complaint_count could overtake billing_support. Also, if qualitative research indicates billing complaints are driven primarily by misunderstanding rather than product limits, a messaging fix might suffice instead of product changes.
memo.title: Prioritize billing/support: address free‑tier restrictions first
